name: HVG Dealer goAML/RMCP Annual Compliance Pack for small jewellers, gold buyers and precious-metal dealers
buyer: Small jewellers, gold and silver buyers and dealers in precious metals and stones, plus other high-value goods dealers (coins, antiques, art, motor dealers) with items of R100,000 or more
trigger: FICA Schedule 1 item 20 (in force 19 Dec 2022): register on goAML, keep an RMCP and resubmit it annually (Directive 12), declare geographic footprint (Directive 10, existing registrants by 31 Oct 2026), file the Directive 7 risk and compliance return, cash reports of R50k or more, suspicious transaction reports, sanctions screening, appoint a compliance officer. Draft PCC 126 (precious metals and stones) issued 30 Sep 2026, comments close 16 Oct 2026.
evidence: https://www.moonstone.co.za/?p=61913 ; https://acts.co.za/news/blog/2026/02/fic-guidance-high-value-goods-dealers ; https://www.golegal.co.za/?p=74912 ; https://www.moonstone.co.za/fic-accepting-rmcps-after-the-12-march-deadline/ ; https://mjkinc.co.za/rmcp ; https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-12-11-know-your-carats-dodge-crooks-cash-in-on-gold-safely.md . Competitor search found only law-firm and consultancy RMCP services and outsourced compliance officers (mjkinc.co.za, golegal.co.za, acpas.co.za); no vertical software for jewellers seen.
existing: Law-firm and consultancy RMCP templates and outsourced compliance officers; FIC goAML (free); no jewellery-specific SaaS found
unchecked: How many small jewellers or gold buyers actually reach the R100k-per-item test (the cap on buyer count); whether the RMCP or footprint deadlines apply to item 20 (sources disagree on 9 vs 31 Oct); SADPMR licence-holder count; whether PCC 126 pulls in second-hand or scrap dealers; pricing of outsourced compliance officers; any jewellery-specific tool.

first_check.duty: Confirmed. FICA Schedule 1 item 20 (high-value goods dealer, R100k or more per item, including linked payments) has been in force since 19 Dec 2022. The duties are: register on goAML, keep and submit an RMCP (all such dealers had to submit RMCPs in March 2025), file the Directive 7 risk and compliance return, do due diligence, file s28 cash reports for R50k or more, s29 suspicious-transaction reports and s28A sanctions reports. Directive 10 geographic disclosure is due by 31 Oct 2026 for existing registrants (per a GoLegal snippet; the page itself returned 403, so I could not check the 9 vs 31 Oct dispute). Draft PCC 126 (issued 30 Sep 2026, comments close 16 Oct 2026) covers miners through retailers and secondary-market traders. It requires a separate registration for each SADPMR authorisation (jeweller's permit, diamond dealer licence and others). It does not say whether scrap or second-hand gold buyers are covered. Penalties: FIC fines from R10k, about 90% of motor-dealer penalties are R100k or more, and fines can reach about R500k (nCino KYC, via FAnews).
first_check.market: Unverified. I found no FIC count of item 20 registrants and no SADPMR count of jeweller's permit holders. A 2021 SADPMR presentation reported 1,584 licences issued in total over 2015/16 to 2019/20, which is not a permit count. Motor dealers are the largest item 20 group ("dozens" sanctioned). How many small jewellers or gold buyers meet the R100k-per-item test is unknown, and probably only a few hundred to low thousands.
first_check.competitor: No software built for jewellers or gold dealers found. Partial overlap: nCino KYC (formerly KYC Africa) markets due-diligence checks, Home Affairs and CIPC verification and watchlist screening to high-value goods dealers. Moonstone offers a do-it-yourself FICA compliance package (gap analysis, goAML help, RMCP customisation). ClearComply (from R99/month) tracks FICA registration deadlines but shows no RMCP or goAML features. RMCP services and outsourced compliance officers come from mjkinc, golegal and acpas. goAML itself is free.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Under FICA Schedule 1 item 20 (in force since 19 Dec 2022), anyone selling an item worth R100k or more must register on goAML, keep and submit an RMCP, do due diligence, file cash reports from R50k and suspicious-transaction reports, and screen for sanctions. FIC fines start at R10k, and most fines on motor dealers are at least R100k. Draft PCC 126 (30 Sep 2026, comments close 16 Oct) brings in precious-metal and stone dealers, with one FIC registration per SADPMR permit. Nobody offers a jeweller-specific product. But nCino KYC already sells due-diligence and watchlist screening to high-value goods dealers, Moonstone has a do-it-yourself FICA pack, and law firms sell RMCP services. The buyer count is unknown, and the R100k-per-item test leaves out many small jewellers. Draft guidance remains draft.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial substitutes: Moonstone FICA Toolkit (one-off R4,995 RMCP template, with no bullion-dealer template); nCino KYC and DocFox (generic KYC and sanctions screening); Gold Manager Pro (buy-back ID scanning and police reporting, not FICA); law-firm and consultancy RMCP services. Unverified: number of registered high-value goods dealers (no sector count found; FIC had 51,020 registered institutions in total at 31 March 2024, according to a secondary summary); whether the September 2026 RMCP directive names item 20 (the acts.co.za summary does not list it); whether PCC 126 covers scrap gold buyers.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills it, but it remains weak. No software built for jewellers or gold dealers covers RMCP, goAML, cash reports and annual RMCP resubmission together. The closest substitutes cover only part of the job. Moonstone's FICA Toolkit is a one-off R4,995 RMCP template, and Moonstone told one commenter it has no bullion-dealer template. nCino KYC and DocFox offer generic KYC and screening. Gold Manager Pro (on Capterra) handles buy-back ID scanning and police reports but not FICA. The duty does bite: a September 2026 directive sets annual October RMCP cut-offs, and draft PCC 126 puts SADPMR permit holders in scope. Two things hold the score down. Only dealers selling single items of R100k or more qualify, and I found no count of registered high-value goods dealers. Consultancies already serve this group cheaply.
